clue.text: See 14
See 6
Very dangerous obstacle, half incomplete

parts.note: a let is an old word for a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

indicators.note: incomplete says the word half is missing its final letter

parts.note: the word half itself, taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A hazard warning about a barrier that is only partly finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lethal can kill, so it is extremely dangerous; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Process of breaking up staff allowance

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff of office
a ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies

explanation.surface: A bureaucratic phrase about dismantling an employee benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up staff allowance' reads as cutting a perk; the definition is the first four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Maceration is softening something into pieces by soaking, a physical breaking down.

clue.text: Cacophony from infant, school's ending

parts.note: a babe is a baby or infant

indicators.note: ending asks for the last letter of the word school's

explanation.surface: A noise complaint about a toddler at the end of the school day.
explanation.walkthrough: BABEL, after the biblical tower where languages were confused, now means a din of voices.
explanation.definitionFit: A babel is a confused noise of many voices, so a cacophony.

clue.text: Cheers erupting at first in rejection of loud music, so lifted

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the reversed music word
rejection here means turning the word for loud music back on itself

parts.note: punk is loud, aggressive rock music

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of erupting

explanation.surface: A crowd's applause at a gig breaks out while punk is being turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' reverses the loud music to give KNUP, and 'in' sets the E inside that run. 'Cheers' is British thanks, not applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken up can mean raised or lifted, as a hem or carpet is taken up.

clue.text: Pride of lions hurry up taking "Pride's Tail" for working title

indicators.note: taking means the next letter is added on at the end
in a down entry, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lion's mane is its glory, wittily its pride
to dart is to hurry

indicators.note: Tail asks for the last letter of Pride's

explanation.surface: A film called Pride's Tail gets a working title about a pride of lions in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: One 'up' turns both pieces, giving TRADENAM. The quoted "Pride's Tail" poses as a film title but just supplies a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name is the name a business trades under, a title used for work.

clue.text: 19 20 character, suit on, nerd's coat ragged

parts.note: kind means nature or character, as in 'of a kind'
hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

indicators.note: ragged says the letters of on, nerd's and coat are torn up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A costume note about a geek's tattered jacket worn over a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: '19 20' points to EALING COMEDY; this 1949 film is one. 'ragged' rearranges ONNERDSCOAT into ANDCORONETS.
explanation.definitionFit: This title is a celebrated black comedy made by Ealing Studios, an example of the category.

clue.text: Little movement at sea, waves painted white, ultimately

indicators.note: waves as a verb means the letters of painted are swirled about
ultimately picks the final letter of white

explanation.surface: A seascape description: calm water, waves picked out in white paint.
explanation.definitionFit: At neap tide the range between high and low water is smallest, so the sea moves little.

clue.text: 19 20 throughout screening left first coil to be fixed

indicators.note: screening means the Latin word encloses the next pieces, like a screen around them

parts.note: passim is Latin for throughout, used in footnotes
port is the left side of a ship
top means first, as in top of the class

indicators.note: to be fixed says the letters of coil need sorting into a new order

explanation.surface: A projectionist's note: a reel coil has to be fixed before the screening.
explanation.walkthrough: '19 20' is EALING COMEDY, this being a 1949 film. 'to be fixed' turns COIL into LICO.
explanation.definitionFit: This title is a 1949 film from Ealing Studios, one example of the category.

clue.text: Upper chamber dry, stopping perfect circulation, primarily

indicators.note: stopping means the dry piece plugs the middle of the perfect piece

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or perfect, written here as AI
TT, teetotal, means not drinking, dry

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of circulation

explanation.surface: A note about a dry room where airflow is cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room right under the roof, the uppermost chamber of a house.

clue.text: Skulls fall quietly in bars

indicators.note: in puts the fall and the quiet letter inside the bars

parts.note: to bar is to ban, so bars means bans
rain is a fall from the sky
p, piano, is the musical mark for quietly

explanation.surface: Drunks cracking their heads by falling over in pubs without a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like pubs; it is a verb meaning bans.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainpan is the skull, the bony case holding the brain.

clue.text: Food server still laid back, about to have some bread

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes round the rest
laid back says the word for still is laid down reading backwards

parts.note: still means yet, as in 'still waiting'
to have food is to eat it
a roll is a small piece of bread

explanation.surface: A relaxed waiter is about to have a bite of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid back' looks like relaxed; it reverses YET to TEY, which goes about EATROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea trolley is a wheeled cart from which food and drink are served.

clue.text: Put foot down, knocking over parrots and budgies?

indicators.note: knocking over means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: parrots and budgies are examples of pets, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone stamps their foot and knocks over the birdcages.
explanation.definitionFit: To step is to put a foot down when walking.

clue.text: Bloody paparazzo finds swimmer

parts.note: bloody means red, the colour of blood
a snapper is informal for a photographer, as a paparazzo is

explanation.surface: A tabloid photographer stumbles on a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' is a fish here: red snapper is a food fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The red snapper is a fish, and a swimmer is a crossword way of saying fish.

clue.text: Lord in Bethlehem's desecrated outside toilet in 19 20

indicators.note: outside says the shuffled letters go round the toilet
desecrated says the letters of Lord, in and Bethlehem are violated and shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, the possessive giving no letter
lav is short for lavatory, a toilet

explanation.surface: A shocking report of a holy place in Bethlehem defiled by a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: '19 20' is EALING COMEDY. 'desecrated' rearranges LORDINBETHLEHEM round LAV; the second 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This title is a 1951 film made by Ealing Studios, one of its famous comedies.

clue.text: Speech in clue too complicated

indicators.note: complicated says the letters of in, clue and too are tangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the wording of a clue is too convoluted.
explanation.definitionFit: Elocution is the art of clear speech, so a fair synonym for it.

clue.text: Able to draw clear in spelling

indicators.note: in puts the clear word inside the spelling word

parts.note: spelling as casting spells means magic
to clear a profit is to net it

explanation.surface: A child who can draw well and spell clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' looks like orthography; it is casting spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetic object can draw iron towards it, so it is able to attract.

clue.text: Slowly approach rear of aggressive dog, put out having swallowed ecstasy

indicators.note: rear of picks the final letter of aggressive
having swallowed means the ecstasy letter is taken inside
out says the letters of dog and put are rearranged

parts.note: E is the common abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A vicious dog is put down after eating a drug pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like put down; only 'out' signals the rearrangement of DOGPUT, which takes E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge up to is to creep closer by small steps, approaching slowly.

clue.text: See 6
Picture a fish overcoming poison through cure, heading off

indicators.note: through means these pieces run through the middle of the cure word
heading off removes the first letter of the word for cure

parts.note: a remedy is a cure

indicators.note: in a down entry, overcoming means the fish sits above the poison

parts.note: ling is a sea fish
CO is carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas

explanation.surface: A recipe for curing a fish that has been poisoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing Studios in London made a famous run of comedies; with 20, the answer is the theme. 'heading off' cuts REMEDY to EMEDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a film, and an Ealing comedy is a kind of film.

clue.text: See 19
Scottish vegetable born before pea, say

parts.note: nee marks a woman's maiden name, meaning born

indicators.note: say means the word pea is spoken, giving the sound of a letter

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like P

explanation.surface: A gardener's note about a vegetable planted before the peas.
explanation.walkthrough: NEEP is the Scots word for a turnip or swede, as in 'neeps and tatties'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland neep is the everyday name for a swede or turnip.

clue.text: Bay here brown, a mare initially covered in droppings

indicators.note: covered in means the brown, a and m pieces sit inside the droppings

parts.note: guano is bird or bat droppings
tan is a light brown

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of mare

explanation.surface: A brown mare at a bay gets splattered with bird mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' looks like a horse's colour next to brown and mare; it is a sea bay, and 'here' points to the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Guantanamo Bay is a bay in Cuba, so the place is where the bay is.

clue.text: Niches getting a lack of endorsements?

parts.note: no means none, a lack of
OKs are approvals or endorsements

explanation.surface: Wondering why some small nooks get no approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Nooks are small recesses or corners, which is what niches are.

clue.text: Corporations up for filth

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a large belly, and tums are bellies

explanation.surface: Big businesses rising up in favour of obscenity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporations' looks like companies; it is jokey slang for paunches.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is dirt or soot, and by extension indecent material, so filth.

clue.text: See 8
Cool attitude, one maintained

indicators.note: maintained means the numeral is held within the attitude word

parts.note: a pose is a bodily attitude or posture
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone keeps up a calm, laid-back stance.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise is calm self-possession, the noun sense of keeping one's cool.

clue.text: Stuff in blue cube that's fried

indicators.note: in puts the rout inside the blue

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so Con
to stuff an opponent is to rout them, beat them heavily

explanation.surface: A recipe filling a cube of blue cheese and frying it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like filling; it is to thrash, ROUT. Con is short for a member of the Conservatives, Britain's party whose colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of bread fried crisp, served in soup.

clue.text: Beginning to sleep rough, becoming underweight

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of sleep

parts.note: craggy means rugged or rough

explanation.surface: Someone starts sleeping rough and grows thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraggy describes someone thin and bony, so underweight.
